name: False Cause
shortDef: Treating a correlation between two things as proof one causes the other.
definition: Concluding that A causes B because the two tend to occur together, without ruling out a third factor that drives both, the cause running the other way, or plain coincidence.
howToSpot: Is the evidence just that two things go together across people, places or times?
Could a third factor explain both, or could the cause run the other way?
Was anything assigned at random or compared with a fair control group?
classicExample: Towns that sell more ice cream have more drownings, so ice cream must make swimming dangerous.
legitimateVersion: A correlation is a fair clue worth investigating. It becomes good evidence of cause when a randomized trial or a careful comparison rules out hidden factors and reverse causation.

contrast.fal_post_hoc: False cause reads cause into things that go together across many cases; post hoc reads cause into one thing simply following another in time.
contrast.fal_texas_sharpshooter: False cause misreads a real correlation; the sharpshooter hunts through data for a cluster and then treats it as meaningful.
